note: P4 for sg-miles-card: forty-one interpretation forks over the six card programmes of this subject. Every one of the ten documents in the P1 bundle supplies at least one quoted fork, compiled from the six encoder reports and verified against both the source texts and the encodings. FOUR THINGS A READER NEEDS. (1) NONE IS MATERIALISED. Every entry is 'resolved-at-encode': each encoder took a reading on its own argument and recorded the alternative, and no fork was threaded as an Interpretation field, so there is no interpretation_type and the R4 1:1 map has nothing to bind. The BNA smoke and the Jersey charities cleanroom likewise materialised none of their twelve, though each of those delegated two to a fact-supplier and this register delegates none: on a contract corpus every fork was taken by the encoder outright. (2) THE SUBJECT IS CONTRACT, NOT LEGISLATION, so 'statutory-wording' is read here as 'wording of the instrument' — the schema's kind vocabulary was fixed on a statute and the other three values needed no stretching. There is no 'instrument' document in the P1 bundle (every T&C is made under a parent cardmember agreement that could not be fetched), so the subject-against-instrument check P4 owes cannot run on this subject; the cross-document forks below are between a T&C and its own FAQ instead. (3) QUOTES ARE EXTRACTED, NOT TYPED. Every source.quote was pulled from the .txt beside the PDF by a script that fails if the text is absent, with whitespace normalised because the pdftotext -layout extraction pads table columns. Citations quoting further text quote it the same way. (4) WITNESSES ARE ONLY CLAIMED WHERE THEY EXIST. divergence 'observable' carries a witness only where the named illustration and its assertion were both found in the module on this branch; where the readings plainly disagree but nothing in the tree exhibits it, divergence is 'unassessed', which is honest at P4 time and is what stops a report claiming interpretation-independence it never measured.

readings.rejection_rationale: It would make the reward fall for the very cardmembers who spent more at SimplyGo, where 7(a) pays 9.5 and 7(b) pays 26: the replacement reading gives 26 where the additive reading gives 35.5, and produces a headline rate that matches no figure printed anywhere in the document.

taken.rationale: Taken on the arithmetic of the document's own cap, which is stated in POINTS and therefore needs no conversion: 28,800 yuu Points divided by 35 bonus points per S$1 is S$822.86 of monthly bonus-earning spend, and 35 is 9 + 26 on the additive reading and on no other. witnesses: `a groceries run at Cold Storage` in `a month above the threshold` — `points per dollar` EQUALS 36, the additive sum 1 + 9 + 26; the replacement reading answers 27
the same call's `status` EQUALS Unconfirmed, against `a month below the threshold`'s Verified — the one place the module declares the summation is its own and not the document's
notes: Direction of error if the taken reading is wrong: the module OVERSTATES, reporting 10.08 miles per dollar where the replacement reading gives 7.56.
This is the ambiguity the encoder flagged for overrule: it is the only condition applied anywhere in the module that no clause states.

ONE OF THE TWO SUPPORTS HAS SINCE BEEN WITHDRAWN. The first pass also argued from miles: 36 points at 8,000/28,800 came to a round 10.0 miles per dollar, offered as a second figure landing on the additive reading. That ratio was rejected when the conversion fork was ruled on 2026-09-21 (see F-yuu-conversion-floor), and at cl.12's 0.28 the same 36 points give 10.08, which is round in nothing. source.quote: 1 yuu Point is equivalent to 0.5% cash rebate or 0.28 miles or more, depending on the redemption item on the yuu Rewards catalogue.

citations.cite: DBS yuu Card T&C (updated on 7 August 2026) cl.12, the clause that states the conversion: "1 yuu Point is equivalent to 0.5% cash rebate or 0.28 miles or more, depending on the redemption item on the yuu Rewards catalogue."

DBS yuu Card T&C (updated on 7 August 2026) cl.7, the clause that prices the monthly cap twice in one parenthesis: "Total Bonus Rewards is capped at 28,800 yuu Points (worth up to S$144 cash rebates or 8,000 miles) per calendar month."

readings.description: cl.12's 0.28 is the conversion, and cl.7's "8,000 miles" is a rounded illustration of the same cap. 28,800 points at 0.28 is 8,064 miles, which the parenthesis's own "worth up to" signals it has rounded down to a round number.

citations.cite: DBS yuu Card T&C (updated on 7 August 2026) cl.12 — the operative sentence: it is the clause that states the conversion, it states one figure, and it is held

DBS yuu Card T&C (updated on 7 August 2026) cl.7 — within the same parenthesis the cash limb is exact (28,800 at 0.5% is S$144 precisely) while the mile limb is not (28,800 at 0.28 is 8,064, printed as 8,000), which is what distinguishes a stated equivalence from a rounded illustration

readings.description: cl.7's pairing of 28,800 yuu Points with 8,000 miles is an exact equivalence, so one yuu Point is 8,000/28,800 = 0.2777... miles and cl.12's 0.28 overstates the conversion by about 0.8 per cent.
readings.rejection_rationale: cl.7 is a clause about the cap and its mile figure is a round number inside a parenthesis introduced by "worth up to"; cl.12 is the clause that states the conversion. The exactness claim fails on its own terms, because 28,800 at 0.28 is 8,064 while the cash limb of the same parenthesis is exact, so it is the mile figure that has been rounded. A figure below a floor is also not consistent with the floor: 0.2777 is less than the 0.28 cl.12 gives as a minimum, and the first pass had that inequality backwards.

taken.rationale: RULED BY THE CONDUCTOR, 2026-09-21, reversing the first pass. The first-pass encoding took cl.7's ratio and reasoned that 0.2777 sat "just below cl.12's 0.28, consistent with 'or more'"; the cross-module cases file, whose assertions were deliberately written to state cl.12's floor rather than quietly adopt cl.7's ratio, is what exposed the difference. Note what the taken reading imports: cl.12 states 0.28 as a MINIMUM ("or more, depending on the redemption item"), so the figure reported is the floor of a range rather than a point value, and the module records the conversion status as Verified against that clause.

witnesses: `yuu cl.6 -- S$100 of groceries at Cold Storage` in `a month with nothing spent yet` (miles-card-cases.l4) — `miles per point` AT LEAST 0.28, which holds at cl.12's figure and fails at cl.7's 0.2777
the same case's `miles per dollar` AT LEAST 2.8 — the same divergence carried through to the headline rate
notes: An intra-document contradiction, and the only one in this corpus that is arithmetical rather than verbal: the two clauses of one document disagree by about 0.8 per cent, and on the rejected reading no redemption priced off cl.7's own cap could reach the floor cl.12 promises.
Direction of error if the taken reading is wrong: the module OVERSTATES miles by about 0.8 per cent.

Recorded as status 'resolved' rather than 'settled' although a ruling exists. The schema reserves 'settled' for an authority — a court or regulator whose word settles — and a project conductor is not one; naming the conductor in settled_by would tell a reader sizing exposure that the underlying question is closed when it is not.
The ruling moves the headline yuu rate from 10.0 to 10.08 miles per dollar and withdraws one of the two supports recorded for F-yuu-bonus-additive, which is noted there.

readings.description: The condition is treated as satisfied and is not tested: the PAssion POSB Debit Card is a Mastercard product, so every transaction this module is asked about is charged to Mastercard. The limitation travels as a condition string on every answer.

citations.cite: PAssion POSB Debit Card 'Up to 9% Cash Rebates (18X yuu Points)' Promotion T&C (updated as of 30 May 2025) cl.4 — the requirement is about the card's network, a property of the card rather than of the individual purchase, and the promotion is offered on a single card product

readings.description: The requirement is a per-transaction test that must be evaluated, so a charge routed other than over Mastercard earns nothing under the promotion.
readings.foreclosure: No fact in the domain records a transaction's card network, so the condition cannot be evaluated and the module does not test it. This is a gap in the fact model forcing the reading, not an argument against the reading.

citations.cite: PAssion POSB Debit Card 'Up to 9% Cash Rebates (18X yuu Points)' Promotion T&C (updated as of 30 May 2025) cl.4 — the condition is written into the definition of Qualified Spend alongside conditions that are plainly per-transaction (local currency, successfully posted)

taken.rationale: Taken because the domain carries no card-network fact and the alternative would make every answer a refusal; the assumption is disclosed on every answer rather than made silently.

notes: Recorded although the choice was forced by a missing fact rather than by the text, because the gap decided a reading: a reviewer needs to see that a stated condition of the promotion is never tested.
Direction of error if the taken reading is wrong: the module OVERSTATES, awarding points on a charge that did not run over Mastercard.
